entries.core_meaning_english: driving away/repelling, and fleeing/scattering in dispersal; also said of a single one

variances.meaning_english: the camel bolted/fled
to drive the camels off in flight

variances.meaning: يريد نكِّل بهم وتمِّم، وهو أن المذنب إذا أذنب وعوقب عليه فقد شُرِّد بتلك العقوبة غيره، لأنه يحذر مثل ما وقع بالمذنب فيَشرُد عن الذَّنب وينسكل
variances.meaning_english: make an example of them so that those behind them are deterred/scattered away — a punished wrongdoer's penalty scares others off from the same offense
variances.citation: قوله جل ثناؤه (آية قرآنية)

entries.core_meaning: الشين والزاي والغين ليس بشيء
entries.core_meaning_english: not a valid (meaningful) root

variances.meaning: يقولون إنه الضُّفْدَع، وهذا مما لا معنى له
variances.meaning_english: said to mean 'frog', but this is meaningless

entries.notes: Appears under the heading باب الشين والزاي وما يثلثهما.

entries.core_meaning: الشين والزاي والنون أصلٌ واحد يدل على امتداد في شيء
entries.core_meaning_english: extension/stretching in a thing

variances.meaning_english: a rough/hard piece of ground called shazan
a thing stretching/extending out

variances.meaning: أي ناحية، فهو قريب من الذي ذكرناه
variances.meaning_english: he slipped aside/away from the abode — related to the sense of extension/direction
variances.citation: قال ابن أحمر: فلا يَرمِينَ عن شَزَنٍ حَزينا (القراءة الأخيرة للكلمة غير مؤكدة تماماً في المسح)

variances.meaning: يقولون إنه الإعياء من الكَلَفاء (أو الجفاء بحسب الحاشية)، وذلك مما يشتد على الإنسان
variances.meaning_english: exhaustion from hardship/toil, something that afflicts a person severely

entries.notes: Footnote flags a textual variant/uncertainty in the last word of the ابن أحمر citation and in الكلفاء/الجفاء; both kept as printed with the alternate noted.

entries.core_meaning: الشين والزاي والباء ليس بأصل، لأنه من باب الإبدال
entries.core_meaning_english: not an independent root — a phonetic substitution (ibdāl) of another root

variances.meaning: يقال للشيء اليابس: شَزَب، والزاي مبدلة من السين، وقد ذُكر في موضعه
variances.meaning_english: said of something dry/withered; the zāy here substitutes for a sīn (i.e. it is a variant of shazab with sīn)
a hard/tough place (footnote: i.e. dry)

entries.core_meaning: الشين والزاء والراء أصل صحيح منقاس يدل على انفتال فى الشىء عن الطريقة المستقيمة
entries.core_meaning_english: a twisting/wrenching of a thing away from the straight, proper course

variances.meaning_english: he looked at him from the corner/tail of his eye, in hostility
a thrust/stab that is not smooth/regular in its manner
a rope twisted toward the left
he ground with the millstone moving his hand away to the right side
variances.citation: قول أبى عبيد

variances.meaning_english: he ground moving his hand away to the left side
variances.citation: قول أبى عبيد

entries.core_meaning: الشين والسين والعين يدلّ على أمرين: الأوّل قلّة والآخر بُعْد
entries.core_meaning_english: two meanings: scarcity/paucity, and distance/remoteness

variances.meaning_english: he has a small/scant amount of wealth
variances.citation: قول العرب

variances.meaning: ولعلّ شِسْعَ النَّعل من ذلك، لقلّته
variances.meaning_english: the sandal-thong (shis'), said to derive from the 'scarcity' sense for its slenderness
the far/distant one; the abode became distant
a horse having a gap between its front teeth
variances.citation: ذكره ابن دريد؛ ذكر أن كلمة إن صحت فهى من القياس

entries.notes: The horse-teeth usage is flagged in the text itself as reported from Ibn Duraid, with the author noting it fits the pattern only if authentic.

entries.core_meaning: الشين والسين والفاء يدلّ على قَحَل ويُبْس
entries.core_meaning_english: aridity and dryness

variances.meaning_english: a parched, dried-out thing
verb: to become dry/withered
dried/jerked meat that is nearly fully dry

entries.core_meaning: الشين والسين والباء هو من الذى قبله
entries.core_meaning_english: this root belongs with/derives from the meaning of the preceding root (dryness)

variances.meaning_english: the bow(-wood) was cut and left until its stave withered/dried

entries.core_meaning: شَبْرَقْتُ اللَّحْمَ: إذا قطَّعْتَه، فالقاف منه زائدة، كأنّك قطّعته شِبْراً شِبْراً
entries.core_meaning_english: to cut something up (the qaf is an extra letter added to the base 'span'-cutting sense)

variances.meaning: إذا قطّعتَه، كأنّك قطعته شِبْراً شِبْراً
variances.meaning_english: I cut up the meat, as if cutting it span by span
I tore/shredded the garment

entries.core_meaning: تكملة من صفحة سابقة: يذكر مشتقات زائدة على ثلاثة أحرف مبدوءة بالشين وترجع إلى معنى شمّر (الخفة والقوة والتفرق في الأمر)
entries.core_meaning_english: continuation: extended (more-than-triliteral) shin-words traced back to the root shamara (lightness/vigor in doing a thing)
entries.notes: Continuation of appendix chapter 'ماجاء من كلام العرب على أكثر من ثلاثة أحرف وأوله شين'. Page ends with closing marker 'تم كتاب الشين'. Footnote (1) marks '[الفتى القوي من الإبل]' as a supplement from al-Mujmal. The شمنصير entry closes with 'والله أعلم بصحتها' (omitted from prior extraction, restored here); footnote (2) attributes the verse to Saʿida ibn Juʾayya al-Hudhali per al-Sukkari's commentary.

variances.meaning: وهو القصير من الرجال، والميم فيه زائدة كأنه في قدر الشِّبْر
variances.meaning_english: a short man; the mim is an added letter, as if it is the size of a shibr (a hand-span)

variances.meaning: وهو الرجل الخفيف في أمره، ويقال الفتى القوي من الإبل. وأيَّ ذلك كان فهو من شَمَر
variances.meaning_english: a man light/quick in his affairs; also said of a strong young camel; either way it derives from shamara

variances.meaning: الأصابع بلغة الحميريين، فِعْل قياسهم غير قياس سائر العرب، ولا معنى للشغل بذلك
variances.meaning_english: 'fingers' in the Himyarite dialect - their derivational pattern differs from the rest of the Arabs, not worth pursuing

variances.meaning: اسم وُضِع وضعاً (لا اشتقاق له)، وهو موضع؛ ويختم الشاهد بـ«والله أعلم بصحتها»
variances.meaning_english: an arbitrarily-coined name with no derivation, and it is a place-name; the citation closes with 'God knows best its accuracy'
variances.citation: مستأرضاً بين بطن الليث أيمنه ... إلى شمنصير غيثاً موصلاً موجا (بيت شعر منسوب لساعدة بن جؤية الهذلي، حاشية 3)
